Find the 4-6 BIGGEST problems in HEALTHCARE / PHARMA & BIOTECH OPERATIONS / LIFE-SCIENCES / PAYERS that are (1) SOFTWARE-ONLY and NON-CLINICAL (no medical device, no diagnosis, no physical, no human trials — admin/ops/data/workflow problems), (2) buildable with today's AI/software by a small team, (3) cost the industry BILLIONS/year (cite), (4) UNDER-served (name competitors honestly), (5) note regulatory load (HIPAA etc.) and prefer lower-regulation workflow/ops problems.

handback.t:
Report written to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\problems-health.md. It has full per-problem detail, source URLs and A/B/C grades. I did not open the primary papers for the Premier, Health Affairs, Gee & Spiro, JAMA directory or IQVIA figures; they came through trade press, press releases and summaries, so verify before quoting.

**Four recommended problems (all software-only and non-clinical):**

1. **Claim denials, appeals and silent-denial recovery (provider side).**
   - Cost: $19.7B (2022) rising to $25.7B (2023) spent fighting denials. About 15% of claims are denied and 54% of those are eventually overturned. Source: Premier survey of 516 hospitals via Becker's and Chief Healthcare Executive, grade B.
   - Competitors: crowded. Waystar, AKASA ($205M raised), Amperos, Infinitus, Fathom and CodaMetrix (coding), and Epic/Oracle native tools.
   - Gap: small practices, specialty niches, and patient-facing appeals.
   - Regulation: medium-high (HIPAA).
   - Difficulty: medium, no breakthrough needed.
   - Time to MVP (my estimate): about 3-4 months for a PDF-in, appeal-out wedge.
   - Sub-problems: six are broken out in the file (denial classification, pre-submission prediction, appeal packet assembly, deadline and ROI tracking, underpayment detection, patient-facing appeals).

2. **Prior authorization and drug utilization-management admin. This is the largest cost and the hardest to enter.**
   - Cost: $93.3B a year for drug utilization management: payers $6.0B, manufacturers $24.8B, physicians $26.7B, patients $35.8B. Source: Health Affairs study via Modern Healthcare, grade B.
   - Burden: AMA late-2024 survey of 1,000 physicians found 39 requests per physician per week and 13 staff hours per week.
   - Tailwind: CMS-0057-F requires payers to run four FHIR APIs, including prior authorization, by 2027-01-01.
   - Competitors: Cohere Health ($200M raised), CoverMyMeds and Surescripts (from my background knowledge, not verified this session), Availity, Infinitus, Waystar, Epic.
   - Regulation: high.
   - Difficulty: high on distribution and integration. Portal automation is brittle.
   - Sub-problems: seven are broken out in the file.

3. **Provider data accuracy: directories, credentialing, enrollment. This is the best low-regulation option.**
   - Cost: only $2.76B (CAQH 2019 practice survey, grade B) and about $4B of industry spend (grade B/C) are cleanly cited.
   - Weak figures: the "$17B" and "$2B credentialing" numbers are blog-grade (C), and vendor per-day lost-revenue figures contradict each other.
   - Competitors: CAQH, Availity, Ribbon, Madaket, Medallion, Verifiable, Modio, CertifyOS, symplr and others.
   - Regulation: low-medium. The data is mostly public (NPPES, state boards).
   - Difficulty: low-medium.
   - Time to MVP (my estimate): about 2-3 months for a verification-and-diff demo.

4. **Pharma rebate, chargeback and 340B duplicate-discount reconciliation (manufacturer B2B).**
   - Cost: "over $20B" duplicate-discount exposure is grade C (blog and vendor framing). IQVIA estimates $34-37.5B of sales "at risk", grade B-, and that is exposure, not realized loss. Treat both as upper bounds.
   - Competitors: IQVIA, Model N, IntegriChain, Precision AQ. I also recall Kalderos, Sentrx and Beacon from background knowledge, unverified here.
   - Regulation: low-medium.
   - Barrier: access to claim data and partnerships, more than the AI.

**Watchlist (fails the "billions cited" test on the evidence found):**
- Clinical-trial start-up contracting and budgets: Tufts figures reached via secondary sites are about $55.7K per day direct cost and 5-6 months to start up, with no industry-wide annual figure. Veeva, Florence and Medidata are entrenched.
- MLR review of promotional content: cycles of 40-60 days per piece (vendor sources), no billions figure. Veeva, Aprimo and Vodori are entrenched.

**Out of scope (clinical validation, FDA exposure, GxP validation, or not credibly sourced):**
- AI scribes, clinical decision support, diagnostics and imaging AI, drug discovery.
- Pharmacovigilance case intake (validated GxP and regulatory reporting; cost data is vendor-only).
- Medical coding: the $36B figure is vendor-sourced (grade C) and the $125B figure has no primary source, so do not use it.
- Patient no-shows: the $150B figure is mostly lost revenue, vendor-origin, and the space is crowded.

**Overall ordering by small-team buildability and under-served niche:**
1. Provider data: fastest and cheapest, lowest regulation, modest ceiling.
2. Denials: a narrow wedge, with the biggest proven pain but a crowded top end.
3. 340B reconciliation: needs design-partner data.
4. Prior authorization: biggest and hardest, needs a payer or network partner.

All time-to-MVP, acquirer and rough-value lines in the file are my judgment and labeled as such. Funding totals came from search summaries and were not checked against Crunchbase.
